patients.summary: Retired construction foreman and former 40 pack-year smoker who joins in 2019 with hypertension, stage 2 CKD, BPH, lumbar spondylosis and a urethral stricture. Over seven years he collects chronic bronchitis, Paget disease of the left tibia, JAK2-positive primary myelofibrosis on ruxolitinib, age-related cognitive decline, a resolved L4 radiculopathy, stricture-related hematuria, carotid sinus hypersensitivity, and an ICU stay for hypertensive emergency complicated by nitroprusside cyanide toxicity.

documents.title: New patient request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Bennett phoned about membership. Wife saw our flyer at the library. Old doctor retiring at the end of the year. Wants to transfer before then. Went over the membership agreement and fee; mailed packet. Scheduled new patient visit 9/17 at 9:00. Release signed by fax for prior primary care and for the urologist he saw this month.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records received from prior primary care office, 41 pages.

Problem list on their summary: hypertension; chronic kidney disease stage 2 (albumin in the urine on yearly checks, creatinine around 1.1); BPH with urinary symptoms; lumbar osteoarthritis with radiating leg pain in the past; urethral stricture; tobacco use; remote appendectomy (age 34).

Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime, acetaminophen 500 mg as needed.

Allergies: none known.

Health maintenance: screening colonoscopy 2014, normal, repeat in 10 years. Tdap not documented.

Also enclosed: outside urology operative note 8/12/2019. Cystoscopy with dilation of a bulbar urethral stricture under anesthesia for a weak stream; bladder unremarkable; uncomplicated, voiding well at discharge.

Filed for review at the new patient visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
64M new to the practice, transferring from a retiring PCP. Records reviewed (see outside records 9/10).

HTN: on HCTZ 25 and lisinopril 10 for about ten years. Doesn't check at home. No headaches, chest pain, SOB.
CKD 2: told of protein in the urine a few years back, creatinine has been ~1.1. No NSAIDs other than an occasional ibuprofen years ago; uses Tylenol now.
BPH: tamsulosin at night, gets up once. Stream weak through the spring, which turned out to be the stricture; urology dilated it 8/12 and he says the stream is the best it's been in years.
Back: lumbar arthritis, decades of hauling and framing. Had pain down a leg years ago that settled. Now just stiffness in the mornings, Tylenol a few times a week.

PSH: appendectomy at 34. Cysto with urethral dilation 8/2019.
FH: father MI at 68. Mother had dementia, difficult behaviors toward the end. Older brother has Paget disease of bone.
SH: married. Retired foreman. Smokes about a pack a day since his early twenties, 40 pack-years. Has quit twice for a few weeks. Beer a couple of times a month.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 134/84. Well-appearing, heavyset. HEENT ok. Neck supple, no bruits. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abd soft, nontender, no masses or organomegaly. Ext no edema. Back: mild paraspinal tenderness low lumbar, SLR negative both sides, strength and reflexes symmetric.

A/P
1. HTN, at goal on current regimen. Continue. CMP today.
2. CKD stage 2 with albuminuria. Already on ACE inhibitor. UACR, CMP.
3. BPH / urethral stricture, voiding well post dilation. PSA today with his agreement after talking through pros and cons.
4. Lumbar spondylosis, stable. Acetaminophen PRN, avoid NSAIDs given kidneys.
5. Tobacco: long talk. Not ready to set a date but will think about it over the holidays. Eligible for yearly low-dose CT screening, ordered.
6. HM: Tdap today. HCV and HIV once. Colonoscopy 2014 normal, due 2024. Flu shot when the high-dose arrives.

RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Bennett, your labs are back. Kidney function is about where your old records had it, and the urine protein is mildly up, same as before. Blood count, liver tests, cholesterol, sugar and PSA all look fine. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. Nothing to change. The lung CT scheduling office should call you this week.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu given L deltoid, lot recorded. No prior reactions. Tolerated well, waited 15 min. VIS given.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
Indication: Baseline lung cancer screening. 64-year-old current smoker, 40 pack-years.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or mass. Airways patent. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Low-dose CT chest
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Baseline screening low-dose CT: no nodules, no mass, no other significant findings. Lung-RADS 1. Next annual screen recommended.

documents.title: Result note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Negative baseline screen. Let pt know by portal. Repeat next fall. Keep working on the cigarettes.

documents.title: Mail-order refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Mail-order pharmacy requesting 90-day supplies of HCTZ 25, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4 under our name now that he's transferred. Pended per protocol, BMP 9/17 ok. Sent.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 6 mo f/u HTN/CKD. Taking meds, no side effects. Voiding fine since the dilation. Back the same.
This winter he has had a cough most mornings bringing up white phlegm, clears after the first cigarette and coffee. No fever, no blood, no weight loss. Says his father had the same smoker's cough.
Tobacco: still ~1 ppd. With the virus in the news and grandkids around, he says this is the time. Picked Monday 4/6. Wants to do it cold turkey, declined patch or meds.

O: vitals as charted. Lungs with a few coarse sounds that clear with cough, no wheeze. Heart RRR. No edema.

A/P
HTN at goal, continue. BMP today.
CKD 2 stable.
Morning productive cough in a smoker, likely tobacco related. Quitting is the treatment. Screening CT in October was clean. Call if any blood, fever or weight loss.
Tobacco cessation counseling >3 min, quit date 4/6. Will check in by phone after.
RTC 6 mo or sooner.

documents.title: Smoking cessation check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called as planned. Quit on 4/6 and has not had one since, two weeks today. Irritable the first week, chewing gum and walking the dog. Cough a bit worse the first days, now easing. Encouraged. Quitline number given again. Updated smoking status to former. PCP aware.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Office converting non-urgent visits during the pandemic. Pt was only coming to review the quit, which RN already covered. He is fine to skip; will see him for the Medicare welcome visit in August.

procedures.procedure: Initial preventive physical examination (Welcome to Medicare)

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 74. PR 168 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 418 ms. Normal axis. No ST or T wave abnormality.

documents.title: Initial Preventive Physical Exam
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Welcome to Medicare visit. Turned 65 last month.

Still off cigarettes since April, four months. Morning cough lighter.
Function: independent, drives, does the household projects. No falls. Hearing and vision fine by his report, sees the eye doctor for readers. Lives with wife, one level ranch, no stairs inside.
Depression screen negative. Alcohol unchanged, rare.
Advance directive: wife is health care proxy, will bring a copy.

Exam: vitals as charted. Heart RRR, lungs clear today. Abd benign, no bruit. Ext no edema. Gait normal, rises from chair without hands.
ECG baseline: normal sinus.

Plan
- BP and kidneys stable on the same meds. Labs today.
- AAA screening ultrasound, one time, ordered.
- Lung CT due October-November.
- Shingrix two-dose series this fall with flu shot.
- Colonoscopy due 2024.
- RTC 6 months.

reports.text:
Indication: AAA screening, male former smoker age 65.
Limited ultrasound of the abdominal aorta. The aorta is normal in caliber throughout, maximum diameter 2.0 cm infrarenal. No aneurysm. Iliac bifurcation not well seen due to bowel gas.

documents.title: Result note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Aorta 2.0 cm, normal. No further screening needed. Letter to pt.

documents.body: Masked visit. High-dose flu R deltoid, Shingrix #1 L deltoid. Warned about a sore arm and feeling run down for a day or two with the shingles shot. Dose 2 due Feb-April, reminder set.
